lines: Ils est très gentils.

why.en: Ils is plural, so être must take its plural form.

gloss.en: They are very kind.

lines: Je est fier de toi.

why.en: With je, être takes its je form.

gloss.en: I'm proud of you.

lines: Comment tu t'appelle ?

why.en: With tu, an -er verb ends in -es in writing.

gloss.en: What is your name?

lines: Elle es très sympa avec tout le monde.

why.en: Elle is third person; this is the tu form of être.

gloss.en: She is very nice to everyone.

lines: Mon voisin est américaine.

why.en: Mon voisin is masculine, so the adjective stays masculine.

gloss.en: My neighbor is American.

lines: J'ai un idée géniale.

why.en: Idée is a feminine noun.

gloss.en: I have a great idea.

lines: Le porte est ouverte.

why.en: Porte is a feminine noun.

gloss.en: The door is open.

lines: Donne-moi le main.

why.en: Main is a feminine noun.

gloss.en: Give me your hand.

lines: Mon fils adore la foot.

why.en: Foot (football) is a masculine noun.

gloss.en: My son loves soccer.

lines: C’est le première fois.

why.en: Fois is feminine — première agrees with it too.

gloss.en: It’s the first time.

lines: Je ne comprends non.

why.en: Negating a verb needs ne … with its partner word; non can't fill that slot.
why.ko: 동사 부정은 ne … 짝말이 필요 → non은 그 자리에 못 온다.

gloss.en: I don't understand.

lines: Je ne suis non sûr de la réponse.

why.en: Negating a verb needs ne … with its partner word; non can't fill that slot.
why.ko: 동사 부정은 ne … 짝말이 필요 → non은 그 자리에 못 온다.

gloss.en: I’m not sure about the answer.

lines: Il aimes jouer au foot.

why.en: -es is the tu ending; il takes the third-person ending.

gloss.en: He likes to play soccer.

lines: Elles aime le chocolat.

why.en: Elles is plural, so the verb needs the plural ending.

gloss.en: They like chocolate.

lines: Je travailles demain matin.

why.en: -es is the tu ending; je takes a different one.

gloss.en: I work tomorrow morning.

lines: Tu parle trop vite pour moi.

why.en: With tu, an -er verb ends in -es in writing.

gloss.en: You speak too fast for me.

lines: J'écoutes une chanson française.

why.en: -es is the tu ending; je takes a different one.

gloss.en: I'm listening to a French song.

lines: Ils arrivons bientôt.

why.en: -ons goes with nous; ils needs the third-person plural ending.

gloss.en: They are arriving soon.

lines: Il y est une place libre ici.

why.en: 'There is' is il y + avoir, not être.
why.ko: '~이 있다'는 il y + avoir, être가 아님.

gloss.en: There's a free seat here.

lines: Il y ont six personnes dans la salle.

why.en: Il y a never changes, even before plural things.
why.ko: il y a는 뒤가 복수여도 그대로.

gloss.en: There are six people in the room.

lines: Je voudrait une glace à la vanille.

why.en: This ending belongs to il/elle; je needs its own.
why.ko: 이 어미는 il/elle용 → je 어미가 따로.

gloss.en: I would like a vanilla ice cream.

lines: Je voudrais ajoute quelque chose.

why.en: After je voudrais, the next verb stays in the infinitive.
why.ko: je voudrais 뒤 동사는 원형 그대로.

gloss.en: I would like to add something.

lines: Tu as combien des frères?

why.en: After combien, the article drops and only the bare preposition remains.
why.ko: combien 뒤에는 관사가 빠지고 전치사만 남는다.

gloss.en: How many brothers do you have?

lines: Bonjour madame, comment allez-tu ?

why.en: The verb is in the vous form, so the pronoun must match it.

gloss.en: Good morning, madam, how are you?

lines: Combien ça coûtent?

why.en: Ça is singular, so the verb is singular.

gloss.en: How much does it cost?

lines: J'ai recevu un paquet ce matin.

why.en: Recevoir has an irregular past participle.

gloss.en: I received a package this morning.

lines: J'ai entendé un cri dans la nuit.

why.en: -re verbs like entendre form the participle in -u, not -é.

gloss.en: I heard a scream in the night.

lines: J'ai manger la moitié du gâteau.

why.en: After avoir in the passé composé comes the past participle, not the infinitive.
why.ko: 복합과거 avoir 뒤에는 원형이 아니라 과거분사.

gloss.en: I ate half of the cake.

lines: J'ai découvri un nouveau café.

why.en: Découvrir has an irregular participle, like ouvrir.

gloss.en: I discovered a new café.

lines: Bravo, tu es réussi ton examen !

why.en: Réussir takes avoir in the passé composé.

gloss.en: Bravo, you passed your exam!

lines: Ils ont partis à sept heures.

why.en: Partir is a verb of movement that takes être.

gloss.en: They left at seven o'clock.

lines: Elles sont arrivé en avance.

why.en: With être, the participle agrees with elles (feminine plural).
why.ko: être와 쓰면 과거분사가 elles(여성 복수)에 일치.

gloss.en: They arrived early.

lines: Je suis aller au cinéma hier avec mes amis.

why.en: After être in the passé composé comes the participle, not the infinitive.
why.ko: 복합과거 être 뒤에는 원형이 아니라 과거분사.

gloss.en: I went to the movies yesterday with my friends.

lines: Elle a partie directement chez elle.

why.en: Partir takes être, not avoir.

gloss.en: She went directly home.

lines: Le taxi a arrivé plus vite que prévu.

why.en: Arriver takes être in the passé composé.

gloss.en: The taxi arrived faster than expected.

lines: Je vais répare ta bicyclette.

why.en: In aller + verb, the second verb stays in the infinitive.

gloss.en: I will fix your bicycle.

lines: Ils va habiter près de la mer.

why.en: Ils needs the plural form of aller.

gloss.en: They are going to live near the sea.

lines: Je vas commander une pizza ce soir.

why.en: This is the tu form of aller; je has its own.
why.ko: 이건 aller의 tu 꼴 → je 꼴이 따로.

gloss.en: I'm going to order a pizza tonight.

lines: Elle va découvert la vérité bientôt.

why.en: After va, use the infinitive, not the participle.

gloss.en: She will discover the truth soon.
gloss.ko: 그녀는 곧 진실을 알게 될 거다.

lines: Il ne veut pas venu.

why.en: After vouloir, the verb is in the infinitive.

gloss.en: He doesn't want to come.

lines: Mon frère veux devenir policier.

why.en: Mon frère is il, so vouloir takes its il form.
why.ko: Mon frère는 il → vouloir도 il 꼴.

gloss.en: My brother wants to become a police officer.
gloss.ko: 우리 형은 경찰이 되고 싶어 한다.

lines: Tu veux partagé cette pizza avec moi ?

why.en: After vouloir, the verb stays in the infinitive, not the participle.
why.ko: vouloir 뒤 동사는 과거분사가 아니라 원형.

gloss.en: Do you want to share this pizza with me?

lines: Tu peut me contacter si tu as un problème.

why.en: This is the il form of pouvoir; tu needs its own.
why.ko: 이건 pouvoir의 il 꼴 → tu 꼴이 따로.

gloss.en: You can contact me if you have a problem.

lines: On peuvent transformer cette pièce en bureau.

why.en: On always takes a singular verb.

gloss.en: We can transform this room into an office.
gloss.ko: 이 방을 사무실로 바꿀 수 있다.

lines: Je se lève tôt chaque matin.

why.en: The reflexive pronoun must match je.

gloss.en: I get up early every morning.

lines: Je me lèves à huit heures chaque jour.

why.en: -es is the tu ending; je takes a different one.

gloss.en: I get up at eight o'clock every day.

lines: Je me reposer sur le canapé après le travail.

why.en: After je me, the verb is conjugated, not left in the infinitive.
why.ko: je me 뒤 동사는 원형이 아니라 활용형.

gloss.en: I rest on the sofa after work.

lines: Elle devient furieuse quand on lui dérange.

why.en: Déranger takes a direct object, so the direct-object pronoun is needed.

gloss.en: She becomes furious when disturbed.

lines: On commandons une pizza pour le dîner.

why.en: On takes the il form of the verb, even when it means 'we'.

gloss.en: Let's order a pizza for dinner.

lines: On buvons du thé tous les après-midis.

why.en: On takes the il form of the verb, even when it means 'we'.

gloss.en: We drink tea every afternoon.

lines: On se retrouvent samedi pour le dîner.

why.en: On takes a singular verb, never the plural.
why.ko: on은 단수 동사, 복수 꼴이 아님.

gloss.en: Let's meet on Saturday for dinner.

lines: C'étais vraiment gênant quand il a oublié mon nom.

why.en: This ending belongs to je/tu; ce needs the third-person ending.

gloss.en: It was really embarrassing when he forgot my name.
gloss.ko: 그가 내 이름을 잊었을 때 정말 민망했다.

lines: J'y ai marre d'attendre ici.

why.en: Avoir marre de … is replaced by the pronoun for de-phrases.
why.ko: avoir marre de …는 de 구를 받는 대명사로.

gloss.en: I'm fed up with waiting here.

lines: J'en vais maintenant.

why.en: Going to a place uses the place pronoun (for à …).

gloss.en: I'm going there now.

lines: Je veux absolument en aller.

why.en: Going to a place uses the place pronoun (for à …).

gloss.en: I absolutely want to go.

lines: Je vais détester ce film, j'y suis sûr.

why.en: Être sûr de … is replaced by the pronoun for de-phrases.
why.ko: être sûr de …는 de 구를 받는 대명사로.

gloss.en: I'm sure I'll hate this movie.
gloss.ko: 나 이 영화 싫어할 거야, 확실해.

lines: Je vais calmer le bébé que pleure.

why.en: The relative pronoun is the subject of pleure here.

gloss.en: I'm going to calm the crying baby.

lines: Regarde le produit qui j'ai acheté hier.

why.en: The relative is the object of acheté; j' is already the subject.
why.ko: 관계대명사는 acheté의 목적어 — 주어는 이미 j'.

gloss.en: Look at the product I bought yesterday.

lines: Inès a gardé le cahier qui ils écrivaient des poèmes ensemble.

why.en: The relative means 'in which' (a place); ils is already the subject.
why.ko: 관계대명사가 '그 안에서'(장소) 뜻 — 주어는 이미 ils.

gloss.en: Inès has kept the notebook where they used to write poems together.
gloss.ko: 이네스는 둘이 함께 시를 쓰던 공책을 간직했다.

lines: Il y a une rumeur que circule au bureau.

why.en: The relative pronoun is the subject of circule.

gloss.en: There's a rumor going around at the office.

lines: Nous partirez en voyage en mars.

why.en: -ez goes with vous; nous needs its own future ending.
why.ko: -ez는 vous 어미 → nous 미래 어미가 따로.

gloss.en: We will go on a trip in March.

lines: Je venirai certainement demain.

why.en: Venir has an irregular future stem.

gloss.en: I will certainly come tomorrow.

lines: Ta commande serai prête dans une heure.

why.en: Ta commande is third person; -ai is the je ending.

gloss.en: Your order will be ready in an hour.
gloss.ko: 주문하신 건 한 시간 뒤에 준비될 거예요.

lines: Je prenderai ma revanche un jour.

why.en: Prendre's future stem is the infinitive minus its final -e.
why.ko: prendre의 미래 어간은 원형에서 끝 -e만 뺀 것.

gloss.en: I will get my revenge one day.

lines: Tu pourrait me prêter un peu de ton parfum ?

why.en: This ending belongs to il/elle; tu needs its own.
why.ko: 이 어미는 il/elle용 → tu 어미가 따로.

gloss.en: Could you lend me some of your perfume?
gloss.ko: 네 향수 좀 빌려줄 수 있어?

lines: J’aimerait te revoir bientôt.

why.en: This ending belongs to il/elle; je needs its own.
why.ko: 이 어미는 il/elle용 → je 어미가 따로.

gloss.en: I would like to see you again soon.

lines: Tu pouvrais arrêter la cigarette pour ta santé.

why.en: Pouvoir has an irregular conditional stem.

gloss.en: You could quit cigarettes for your health.
gloss.ko: 건강을 위해 담배를 끊어 보는 게 어때.

lines: Je pense qui tu as raison.

why.en: After je pense, the clause starts with the conjunction, not a relative pronoun.
why.ko: je pense 뒤 절은 관계대명사가 아니라 접속사로 시작.

gloss.en: I think that you are right.

lines: Émilie veut que son code respectera les normes de sécurité européennes.

why.en: Vouloir que is followed by the subjunctive, not the future.
why.ko: vouloir que 뒤에는 미래가 아니라 접속법.

gloss.en: Émilie wants her code to meet European security standards.
gloss.ko: 에밀리는 자기 코드가 유럽 안전 기준을 지키길 원한다.

lines: Hugo veut que son studio est convenable avant la visite de ses parents.

why.en: Vouloir que requires the subjunctive.

gloss.en: Hugo wants his studio to be presentable before his parents' visit.
gloss.ko: 위고는 부모님이 오시기 전에 원룸이 봐줄 만하길 바란다.

lines: Hugo exige que les commandes sont servies avec diligence, même un samedi soir.

why.en: Exiger que requires the subjunctive.

gloss.en: Hugo demands that orders be served promptly, even on a Saturday night.
gloss.ko: 위고는 토요일 저녁에도 주문이 신속히 나가길 요구한다.

lines: Camille a peur que ce manteau la fait grossir sur les photos.

why.en: Avoir peur que is followed by the subjunctive.

gloss.en: Camille is afraid this coat makes her look bigger in photos.
gloss.ko: 카미유는 이 코트 때문에 사진에서 뚱뚱해 보일까 봐 걱정한다.

lines: Après sa longue pause, Camille avait peur que ses réflexes sont rouillés.

why.en: Avoir peur que is followed by the subjunctive.

gloss.en: After her long break, Camille was afraid her reflexes had gone rusty.
gloss.ko: 긴 휴식 뒤 카미유는 반사 신경이 녹슬었을까 봐 두려웠다.

lines: Thomas serait dévasté s'il perdrait ce poste qu'il attendait depuis si longtemps.

why.en: After si in a hypothesis, use the imperfect, never the conditional.
why.ko: 가정의 si 뒤에는 조건법이 아니라 반과거.

gloss.en: Thomas would be devastated if he lost the job he'd waited so long for.
gloss.ko: 토마는 그토록 오래 기다린 자리를 잃는다면 크게 상심할 것이다.

lines: Nicolas rappelle à Paul le jour où ils avaient rentrés trempés du camping.

why.en: Rentrer (to come home) takes être in compound tenses.

gloss.en: Nicolas reminds Paul of the day they came back soaked from camping.
gloss.ko: 니콜라는 폴에게 캠핑에서 흠뻑 젖어 돌아왔던 날을 떠올리게 한다.

lines: Manon rappelle à Inès l'éclipse qu'elles avaient regardés ensemble à travers des lunettes en carton.

why.en: The participle agrees with the direct object placed before it (l'éclipse, feminine singular).
why.ko: 앞에 온 직접목적어(l'éclipse, 여성 단수)에 과거분사가 일치.

gloss.en: Manon reminds Inès of the eclipse they watched together through cardboard glasses.
gloss.ko: 마농은 이네스에게 둘이 판지 안경으로 함께 봤던 일식을 떠올리게 한다.

lines: J'ai cassé mon ongle en ouvrir la porte.

why.en: Here en introduces a gerund, so it needs the -ant form.

gloss.en: I broke my nail opening the door.

lines: Il a eu un choc en apprendant la vérité.

why.en: The -ant form is built on the nous stem of apprendre.

gloss.en: He was shocked when he learned the truth.

lines: Attention en descendu l'escalier.

why.en: The gerund is en + the -ant form, not a past participle.

gloss.en: Be careful going down the stairs.

lines: Tu serais pu m'avertir avant.

why.en: Pouvoir takes avoir in compound tenses.

gloss.en: You could have warned me before.

lines: Manon écrit qu'il y a dix ans, perdre le contact avec Inès lui serait semblé impensable.

why.en: Sembler takes avoir in compound tenses.

gloss.en: Manon writes that ten years ago, losing touch with Inès would have seemed unthinkable to her.
gloss.ko: 마농은 십 년 전이었다면 이네스와 연락이 끊기는 건 상상도 못 했을 거라고 쓴다.

lines: Chloé regrette que quelqu'un soit saccagé les panneaux du parcours.

why.en: Saccager takes avoir, so the past subjunctive uses avoir.
why.ko: saccager는 avoir 동사 → 접속법 과거도 avoir로.

gloss.en: Chloé is sorry that someone vandalised the course signs.
gloss.ko: 클로에는 누군가 코스 표지판을 망가뜨린 게 안타깝다.

lines: C'est moi que ai fait le gâteau.

why.en: In c'est … qui, the relative is the subject of the next verb.
why.ko: c'est … qui에서 관계대명사는 다음 동사의 주어.

gloss.en: I'm the one who made the cake.

lines: C'est papi qui ont fini par réconcilier Julien et sa sœur.

why.en: The verb after qui agrees with papi, which is singular.

gloss.en: It was Grandpa who ended up reconciling Julien and his sister.
gloss.ko: 결국 쥘리앵과 누이를 화해시킨 건 할아버지였다.

lines: Son absence a été remarqué par tous.

why.en: In the passive, the participle agrees with the subject (son absence, feminine).
why.ko: 수동태 과거분사는 주어(son absence, 여성)에 일치.

gloss.en: Her absence was noticed by everyone.

lines: L'air est visible mais essentiel à la vie.

why.en: Air can't be seen; mais sets that against it being essential.
why.ko: 공기는 눈에 안 보인다 — mais가 '꼭 필요하다'와 맞세운다.

gloss.en: Air is invisible but essential to life.
gloss.ko: 공기는 눈에 보이지 않지만 생명에 꼭 필요하다.

lines: Il va accepter la proposition car il n'est pas d'accord.

why.en: He doesn't agree, so he will turn the proposal down.
why.ko: 동의하지 않으니 제안을 받아들이지 않을 것.

gloss.en: He will reject the proposal because he disagrees.
gloss.ko: 그는 동의하지 않아서 그 제안을 거절할 것이다.

lines: Je reste, puisque tu n'as plus besoin de moi.

why.en: You don't need me any more — that's a reason to go.
why.ko: 더는 내가 필요 없다 → 떠날 이유.

gloss.en: I'm leaving, since you don't need me anymore.
gloss.ko: 네가 이제 내가 필요 없으니 나는 갈게.

lines: Il faut rester négatif malgré les difficultés.

why.en: Il faut + malgré les difficultés is advice to keep a good attitude.
why.ko: il faut + 어려움에도 → 좋은 태도를 지키라는 조언.

gloss.en: You have to stay positive despite the difficulties.
gloss.ko: 어려움이 있어도 긍정적인 마음을 지켜야 한다.

lines: La table de jardin est stable, alors Sarah glisse un carton sous un pied.

why.en: Slipping cardboard under a leg is how you fix a wobbly table.
why.ko: 다리 밑에 판지를 끼우는 건 흔들리는 탁자를 고칠 때.

gloss.en: The garden table is wobbly, so Sarah slips a piece of cardboard under one leg.
gloss.ko: 정원 탁자가 흔들려서 사라는 다리 하나 밑에 판지를 끼운다.

lines: Inès allume le bec Bunsen avec un briquet, car les allumettes sont sèches.

why.en: She uses a lighter because the matches won't light.

gloss.en: Inès lights the Bunsen burner with a lighter because the matches are wet.
gloss.ko: 성냥이 젖어서 이네스는 라이터로 분젠 버너를 켠다.

lines: À l'arrivée, Claire doit accélérer pour ne pas bousculer les bénévoles.

why.en: To avoid bumping into people, you slow down.

gloss.en: At the finish, Claire has to slow down so she doesn't knock into the volunteers.
gloss.ko: 결승점에서 클레르는 자원봉사자들과 부딪히지 않으려고 속도를 줄여야 한다.

lines: Il faut ralentir pour ne pas rater le train.

why.en: Not to miss the train, you need to go faster.
why.ko: 기차를 놓치지 않으려면 더 빨리 가야 한다.

gloss.en: We need to speed up so we don't miss the train.
gloss.ko: 기차를 놓치지 않으려면 속도를 내야 한다.

lines: Le dossier est si mince qu'Antoine l'apporte dans une valise à roulettes.

why.en: A wheeled suitcase is for something big and heavy.
why.ko: 바퀴 달린 가방은 크고 무거운 것을 나를 때 쓴다.

gloss.en: The file is so thick that Antoine brings it in a wheeled suitcase.
gloss.ko: 서류가 너무 두꺼워서 앙투안은 바퀴 달린 가방에 넣어 가져온다.

lines: Le moule est tellement neuf que Camille ne peut plus s'en servir.

why.en: She can't use the mould any more because it is damaged.

gloss.en: The mold is so warped that Camille can't use it anymore.
gloss.ko: 틀이 너무 찌그러져서 카미유는 더는 쓸 수 없다.

lines: Thomas craint de recevoir un blâme s'il envoie le bon fichier au client.

why.en: You fear a reprimand only when you make a mistake.

gloss.en: Thomas fears getting a reprimand if he sends the wrong file to the client.
gloss.ko: 토마는 고객에게 엉뚱한 파일을 보내면 질책을 받을까 걱정한다.

lines: Malgré les cartons partout, Nicolas reste stressé et sifflote.

why.en: Whistling, and malgré the mess, point to staying relaxed.

gloss.en: Despite the boxes everywhere, Nicolas stays relaxed and whistles.
gloss.ko: 곳곳에 상자가 있는데도 니콜라는 느긋하게 휘파람을 분다.

lines: En hiver, le chalet de la famille de Sarah devient accessible à cause de la neige.

why.en: Winter snow cuts the chalet off.
why.ko: 겨울 눈 때문에 산장에 갈 수 없게 된다.

gloss.en: In winter, Sarah's family chalet becomes inaccessible because of the snow.
gloss.ko: 겨울에는 눈 때문에 사라 가족의 산장에 갈 수 없다.

lead: Tout le monde le félicite pour son examen.
lines: Il a échoué malgré les difficultés.

why.en: Everyone congratulates him, so he succeeded — malgré marks success despite problems.
why.ko: 모두 축하한다 → 해냈다. malgré는 어려움에도 해낸 것.

gloss.en: He succeeded despite the difficulties.

lead: Je suis rentré à pied sous l'orage.
lines: Mon pantalon est tout sec à cause de la pluie.

why.en: Walking home in a storm, in the rain — the trousers got soaked.
why.ko: 폭풍 속을 걸어왔고 비 때문 → 젖었다.

gloss.en: My pants are all wet because of the rain.

lead: Mes voisins écoutent de la musique très fort.
lines: Je suis calme à cause du bruit.

why.en: Loud music next door is a reason to be annoyed.
why.ko: 옆집 음악이 시끄럽다 → 짜증 날 이유.

gloss.en: I am annoyed because of the noise.

lead: Ce matin, il y a une grosse tempête.
lines: Le vol a été annulé à cause du beau temps.

why.en: A storm gets flights cancelled — that's bad weather.

gloss.en: The flight was canceled due to bad weather.

lead: Je rentre très fatigué tous les soirs.
lines: Ce travail est facile, mais intéressant.

why.en: Coming home exhausted every night means the work is hard.

gloss.en: This work is hard but interesting.

lead: On peut à peine y entrer à deux.
lines: La cabane est grande mais confortable.

why.en: Barely room for two means the hut is small.

gloss.en: The cabin is small but comfortable.

lead: Le petit garçon a cassé son jouet préféré.
lines: Il rit parce que son jouet est cassé.

why.en: A broken favourite toy makes a child cry.

gloss.en: He is crying because his toy is broken.

lead: Les enfants disent que les légumes verts, c'est mauvais.
lines: Les enfants adorent les épinards, alors Louis les cache dans les lasagnes.

why.en: Kids who think green vegetables taste bad refuse them — hence the hiding.
why.ko: 아이들이 초록 채소가 맛없다고 한다 → 안 먹으니 숨긴다.

gloss.en: The children refuse spinach, so Louis hides it in the lasagna.
gloss.ko: 아이들이 시금치를 안 먹으려 해서 루이는 라자냐 속에 숨긴다.

lead: Le facteur doit faire un grand détour tous les jours.
lines: Le facteur est ravi parce que la route du village de Sarah est encore fermée.

why.en: A closed road and a long detour every day are reasons to be annoyed.
why.ko: 길이 막혀 매일 멀리 돌아간다 → 언짢다.

gloss.en: The postman is annoyed because the road to Sarah's village is closed again.
gloss.ko: 사라네 마을로 가는 길이 아직 막혀 있어서 우편배달부는 언짢다.

lines: Je n'aime pas le temps chaud.

why.en: Someone who prefers summer dislikes cold weather.
why.ko: 여름을 더 좋아한다 → 추운 날씨가 싫다.

gloss.en: I don't like cold weather.

lead: Il fait nuit et il n'y a pas de lampe.
lines: La pièce est trop claire pour lire.

why.en: At night with no lamp, the room is dark.

gloss.en: The room is too dark to read.
gloss.ko: 방이 너무 어두워서 책을 읽을 수 없다.

lead: Dans la montagne, mon téléphone ne marchait pas.
lines: Le signal était trop fort pour téléphoner.

why.en: The phone didn't work, so the signal was weak.

gloss.en: The signal was too weak to make a call.
gloss.ko: 신호가 너무 약해서 전화를 걸 수 없었다.

lead: J'ai rempli ce carton de livres.
lines: Ce carton est trop léger à porter seul.

why.en: A box full of books is heavy.

gloss.en: This box is too heavy to carry alone.
gloss.ko: 이 상자는 혼자 들기엔 너무 무겁다.

lines: Il est trop tard pour partir.

why.en: The party has only just started, so it's early to leave.

gloss.en: It is too early to leave.

lead: Quelle bonne surprise, ça fait longtemps !
lines: Je suis triste de te voir.

why.en: A good surprise after a long time — a happy reunion.

gloss.en: I'm happy to see you.

lead: Aujourd'hui, j'ai travaillé du matin au soir.
lines: Je suis très reposé ce soir.

why.en: Working from morning to night leaves you tired.

gloss.en: I am very tired tonight.

lead: Je vais à l'école à pied en cinq minutes.
lines: Mon école n'est pas très près.

why.en: Five minutes on foot means it isn't far.

gloss.en: My school is not very far.

lines: Je suis pour cette idée.

why.en: Finding the plan dangerous means you oppose it.

gloss.en: I am against that idea.

lines: Il est toujours très méchant.

why.en: Always helping the neighbours means he is kind.

gloss.en: He is always very kind.
